Chios
KY-os
proper noun
An isle of the Aegean Sea off the coast of Ionia; a day’s stage on Paul’s swift voyage toward Jerusalem.

📖 Biblical Definition

Chios is an isle of the Aegean lying off the Ionian coast of Asia Minor, over against Smyrna. It is named once, among the day-by-day stages of Paul’s hastening voyage toward Jerusalem: “we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus” (Act 20:15). The apostle was pressing homeward, “for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost” (Act 20:16), and Chios was one of the swift steps of that eager journey — a night over against the island, and on again with the next day’s light. The reckoning of the days is itself a testimony: the Spirit counts them out, one by one, “the next day… the next day.” The LORD numbers the stages of His servant’s haste as surely as the stations of his rest. Let the believer be diligent and eager in the work set before him, redeeming the time and pressing toward the mark; yet let him know that even his hastening is measured out by God, day by appointed day, and not one of them is wasted or unwatched.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An isle of the Aegean off Ionia; a day’s stage on Paul’s hastening voyage toward Jerusalem for Pentecost.

expand to see more

CHIOS, an isle of the Aegean Sea off the Ionian coast of Asia Minor.

It lies over against Smyrna, and is named once in the Scriptures.

It was a day’s stage on Paul’s swift voyage toward Jerusalem.

The apostle hasted to be at Jerusalem by the day of Pentecost.

It witnesses that God numbers the stages of His servant’s haste, day by appointed day.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 20:15 — "And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus."

Act 20:16 — "For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost."

Psa 107:23 — "They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;"

Pro 16:9 — "A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

An isle of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the truth that God numbers the very stages of His servant’s diligent haste, and none is wasted.

expand to see more

Chios faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth it carries answers both the sloth that will not press toward the mark and the anxious haste that reckons its hurried days unwatched and unblessed — as though eager labour ran ahead of God’s reckoning.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God numbers the days of our diligence. The Spirit counts out the stages of Paul’s haste, “the next day… the next day,” as surely as the stations of his rest. The believer presses toward the mark, redeeming the time; yet even his hastening is measured out by God, day by appointed day, and not one of them is wasted or unwatched.
